name: Streaming Field Renamer
description: Renames the fields of the input from rename rules (current name, new name) written in the block or kept in a CSV file, working through the data in chunks so large inputs never have to fit in memory.
introductoryText:
Renames the fields of the input using rename rules written in the block, or kept in a CSV file so the same list of renames can be shared between projects and kept up to date in one place. The block works through the data in chunks (it streams), so it suits very large inputs. Streaming blocks have a single input, which is why the rules are an option rather than a second input.

**How to set it up**: write the rules in **Rename rules**, one per line or separated by semicolons, as `Current Name = New Name`:

```
acct_no = Account Number; txn_dt = Transaction Date
```

Or leave it empty and choose a CSV file with the columns **Current Name** and **New Name**, one rule per field to rename. Rules written in the block take precedence over the file. For example:

```
Current Name,New Name
acct_no,Account Number
txn_dt,Transaction Date
```

- Field names are matched exactly, including capitals; spaces at either end of a name in the rules are ignored, and so are capitals and spaces in the file's two column headings.
- Fields with no rule keep their names; rules naming a field the input doesn't have are ignored.
- Rules with an empty current name (blank lines) are skipped; a name containing `=` or `;` needs the file. The block stops with a message if a rule has no new name, if a current name appears twice, or if renaming would give two fields the same name.

To keep the rules in a data set rather than a file, or to see which rules matched nothing, use the **Field Renamer** block instead.
